title: The two syllables
situation: A man loses his position and finds that the people who filled his house a month earlier no longer answer.
wise_response: The verse does not tell him to chase them. It names the word 'friend' as a shelter in disaster and a medicine for grief, and leaves him to notice who is still there.
why_it_worked: It defines friendship by what it does in the bad season, so the test is the timing of the arrival rather than the warmth of the greeting.
tempting_wrong_answer: Count the people who were present when things were good, and treat the absence as a surprise.
original_text:
kenāmṛtam idaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ mitram ity akṣara-dvayam |
āpadāṃ ca paritrāṇaṃ śoka-santāpa-bheṣajam ||
edition: Ramchandra Jha, 6th ed., Varanasi: Chowkhamba Vidyabhavan, 1991 (Vidyabhavana Sanskrit Grantha Mala 17); GRETIL sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra
ai_translation: By whom was this nectar made — the two syllables 'friend'? It is a shelter from disasters, a medicine for grief and burning sorrow.
translation_notes: AI translation made from the Sanskrit of the Jha edition (GRETIL). No modern scholarly translation consulted. Marked working until two readers of Sanskrit have verified it.

title: A friend in the bad season
situation: A man has to decide whom to trust with something that matters, and everyone around him is agreeable.
wise_response: The verse gives him a test: look for the one who was present when things were bad, and treat the company of prosperity as unproven.
why_it_worked: The test costs the other person something. Agreeableness is free, so it cannot pass a test built on adversity.
tempting_wrong_answer: Trust the most agreeable person in the room.
original_text:
āpat-kāle tu samprāpte yan mitraṃ mitram eva tat |
vṛddhi-kāle tu samprāpte durjano 'pi suhṛd bhavet ||
edition: Ramchandra Jha, 6th ed., Varanasi: Chowkhamba Vidyabhavan, 1991 (Vidyabhavana Sanskrit Grantha Mala 17); GRETIL sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra
ai_translation: A friend at the time of calamity — that alone is a friend. At the time of prosperity, even a wicked man becomes a friend.
translation_notes: AI translation made from the Sanskrit of the Jha edition (GRETIL). No modern scholarly translation consulted. Marked working until two readers of Sanskrit have verified it.

title: The three who break trust
situation: A man has been let down by someone he trusted and is deciding whether to treat it as an ordinary disappointment.
wise_response: The verse names three kinds together — betraying a friend, ingratitude, and destroying confidence — and refuses to treat any of them as small.
why_it_worked: Naming the category makes the harm visible, so it cannot later be excused as a misunderstanding.
tempting_wrong_answer: Call it a private grievance, say nothing, and keep the relationship as it was.
original_text:
mitra-drohī kṛtaghnaś ca yaś ca viśvāsa-ghātakaḥ |
te narā narakaṃ yānti yāvac candra-divākarau ||
edition: Ramchandra Jha, 6th ed., Varanasi: Chowkhamba Vidyabhavan, 1991 (Vidyabhavana Sanskrit Grantha Mala 17); GRETIL sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra
ai_translation: The betrayer of a friend, the ungrateful man, and the destroyer of trust — those men go to hell as long as moon and sun endure.
